sourceNotes: Where Evil Lives describes a mole-like burrower in The Hanging Tree, O5. The publisher’s illustration supplies pale curved tusks and bony back growths. Both printings use the same appearance.
prompt: Paint one compact, low-built, mole-like burrowing beast in restless three-quarter side view. The shape should feel small and dense, with robust front paws and broad dark digging claws, tightly tucked hind legs, charcoal-brown shaggy fur and a cream-gray chest, short pointed muzzle with a dusky nose and alert muted amber eyes. Add two modest upward curving pale tusks, a few short pale bony spurs over the dark upper back, and a pair of slender golden-ivory branched bony horns sweeping backward close to the shoulder and not too wide. Angle its head slightly down as if sniffing. Natural quadruped anatomy and a fringed root-digging silhouette. No cubs, no human-like hands, no roaring pose, no soil scene.
